identity.title: Scrubber Pressure-Drop Log (S-1 acid line, S-2 caustic line) and Weekly C-1 Carbon Outlet Detector-Tube Check, August–September 2026, Portland Facility
identity.issuer: Cascade Specialty Chemicals, LLC (entries by T. Nguyen and K. Sato, line leads)
identity.site: Portland — 4410 NW Front Ave, Portland, Oregon 97210

scan.summary: This is your own monitoring log. It records the checks required by Conditions 3.1 and 3.3 of your Air Contaminant Discharge Permit 26-2841-ST-01: a daily pressure-drop reading on scrubbers S-1 and S-2, and a weekly breakthrough check at the outlet of carbon unit C-1. It is judged on whether it is complete and up to date. It has four problems: operating days with no reading in August, a September 9 reading above the permit range with nothing noted about it, a missing weekly carbon check in September, and no supervisor sign-off.
scan.freshness_note: The last entry is September 25, 2026. That was four days ago. Nothing is entered for Monday, September 28. If the lines ran that day, get the reading or confirm it was taken and not yet entered. The log is otherwise current.

gaps.title: Five August operating days have no scrubber reading
gaps.description: The log's own line counters say the acid line ran 21 days and the caustic line ran 20 days in August, but only 16 rows are entered. There are no entries at all between August 14 and August 24. The weekly carbon check on August 17 shows the site was working that week. That leaves about 5 operating days with no reading for S-1 and 5 for S-2. Condition 3.1 requires a reading every operating day.
gaps.fix: Check whether readings for August 17–21 were taken on paper or another sheet and never copied in. If they were not taken, write a dated note in the log explaining the missed days. Check your permit's deviation and annual-report terms to see whether missed monitoring has to be reported to Oregon DEQ. Consider matching the log against the line counters every week.
gaps.citation: Air Contaminant Discharge Permit 26-2841-ST-01, Condition 3.1 (as quoted in the log header)
gaps.locator: Page 1, August table and throughput note
gaps.quote: August throughput (from the line counters): acid line ran 21 days, caustic line ran 20 days. Rows entered: 16.

gaps.title: September 9 S-2 reading above the permit range, with nothing recorded about it
gaps.description: On September 9 scrubber S-2 read 6.4 inches of water column. The permit range is 2.0 to 6.0. The Notes column is blank: no cause, no corrective action, no time it was back in range. The next day's reading was 4.6.
gaps.fix: Add a dated note giving the cause, what was done (for example, nozzles cleaned), and when the reading came back into range. Check your permit for any requirement to record or report an excursion from a parameter range, and file with Oregon DEQ if it applies. I have not read the permit's reporting conditions, so I cannot say whether a report is required.
gaps.citation: Air Contaminant Discharge Permit 26-2841-ST-01, Condition 3.1. Any reporting duty would be in the permit's own reporting conditions, which I have not seen.

gaps.title: Weekly C-1 carbon outlet check missing for the week of September 14
gaps.description: Condition 3.3 requires a breakthrough check at the C-1 outlet every week. September shows checks only for the weeks of September 7 and September 21. There is none for the week of September 14, even though the lines ran September 14–18. The week of September 28 is still in progress.
gaps.fix: Find out whether the check was done and not written down. If it was not done, note the missed week in the log, consider whether it has to be reported under the permit, and make sure the week of September 28 check gets done.
gaps.citation: Air Contaminant Discharge Permit 26-2841-ST-01, Condition 3.3 (as quoted in the log)
gaps.quote: Condition 3.3: weekly check for breakthrough at the C-1 carbon unit outlet

gaps.title: No supervisor review signature
gaps.description: The form has a line for supervisor review, but it is blank with no date. That leaves no sign that anyone reviewed the log, which may be why the missing days and the 6.4 reading went unnoticed.
gaps.fix: Have a supervisor review both months, record what they find, then sign and date. Make it a monthly review.

deadlines.title: Record the S-1 and S-2 pressure drop each day either line runs
deadlines.source_line: record the pressure drop across each scrubber once per operating day; keep it between 2.0 and 6.0 inches of water column

deadlines.title: Weekly C-1 carbon outlet breakthrough check (week of Sep 28 is still due)
deadlines.source_line: Condition 3.3: weekly check for breakthrough at the C-1 carbon unit outlet

scan.confidence_notes: Both pages were clearly legible. Titles and the permit reference come from the page 1 header; the September data and the blank supervisor line come from page 2. I am confident about the missing August days, because the log's own counter note gives the shortfall. I am also confident about the 6.4 reading and the missing weekly check. I worked out the week in which the August readings are missing (Aug 17–21) from the gap in dates and the August 17 carbon check; that part is inferred. I have not seen the permit itself. I only know Conditions 3.1 and 3.3 as the log describes them. So I cannot say whether the excursion or the missed monitoring has to be reported to Oregon DEQ, or how long these records must be kept. This log is not a version of anything you already hold; it is a record of the conditions in your air permit.
